summary: L-size strategy with good breadth on the mechanism (runs, flattening, heading-level policy, br/li defaults) but it fails on the two things this feature's history says matter most: the AC10 byte-identity gate is not a byte-identity check, and the heading heuristic is specified with positive controls only. Verified facts driving this: (1) grep finds ZERO occurrences of strong/<b>/<em> in tests/test_t_hunted_source.py, tests/test_lamley_source.py and tests/test_autoevolution_source.py, so 'existing tests pass unedited' carries almost no information for those three; (2) code-research II-2.4 states outright that the heuristic MUST be gated per source or orangetrack's tests go red, and that whether orangetrack has whole-bold short paragraphs is UNMEASURED - yet Decision 2 states no gate, the Architecture's three injected callables do not include one, and no listed test would catch it; (3) zero tests in any of the four engine test files reference list_item or _PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES, while Task 4 edits four engines and lists one test file; (4) tests/fixtures/ contains two .py builders and zero HTML - every measured number the spec relies on (24/286 promotions, 14/41/48/50 lamley images, 13/14 misalignment, 73-vs-85 char headroom) is unreproducible in the repo. E2E: None is the right call on live-fetch grounds, but the substitute must be a committed recorded-fixture corpus, not the operator's post-deploy read. Seven strategy items fail the litmus test - they would still pass with the core behaviour removed or inverted.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (Integration tests, 'orangetrack regression: its existing tests pass unedited') + Risks table row 1 + Task 1 Verify-smoke
findings.issue: The AC10 gate is 'existing tests pass unedited', which is not a byte-identity check and passes under real behaviour change. code-research II-8.3 enumerates what the 94 orangetrack tests actually pin: block types for specific hand-written fixtures, runs equality, formats-key omission, no doubled spaces, run locatability, and an exact node tree for ONE end-to-end case. Nothing pins the full rendered node tree for the other fixtures, nothing pins paragraphs exactly for most of them, and no fixture is a real article. Decisively, II-2.4 says the heading heuristic can flip an orangetrack paragraph to heading and that whether orangetrack has such paragraphs today is unmeasured because its feed was never fetched - i.e. the exact drift the gate exists to stop can occur in a shape no assertion covers. Litmus test: strip a genuine behaviour (apply the heuristic, change lead run handling, change image ordering) and this gate still goes green.
findings.recommendation: Add a golden-file gate as Task 1 step 0, BEFORE any code moves. Script: for every HTML fixture embedded in tests/test_orangetrack_source.py plus a committed snapshot of content:encoded pulled once from the live orangetrack feed, run _parse_content_encoded and dump json.dumps({'title','subtitle','paragraphs','blocks','images'}, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) AND telegraph_publisher.preview_nodes(...) for the same input into tests/fixtures/orangetrack_golden.json. Commit that file on the pre-extraction commit. Then new file tests/test_orangetrack_golden.py::test_rendered_output_byte_identical_to_golden re-runs both and asserts string equality per fixture (assert actual == expected on the serialised form, so the diff names the drifting key). Extend Task 1 Verify-smoke to: `git diff --stat tests/test_orangetrack_source.py tests/fixtures/orangetrack_golden.json` must be empty - editing the golden file is itself a gate failure requiring operator sign-off. This is the only construct in which 'byte-identical' is falsifiable.

findings.location: Decision 2 + Architecture ('three injected callables') + Section: Testing Strategy (Unit tests)
findings.issue: The heading heuristic is not gated per source, and no listed test fails when it is applied to orangetrack. code-research II-2.4: 'If the shared emitter applied the rule unconditionally, any orangetrack paragraph that is entirely bold and short would flip paragraph->heading and those tests would go red. So the rule has to be gated per source.' The tech-spec instead makes looks_like_heading part of dom_blocks' shared defaults (Architecture bullet 1), lists only chrome-predicate / image-src picker / video wrapper as per-site injections, and Decision 2 describes the rule with no source condition. orangetrack has no bold->heading behaviour today, so applying it changes orangetrack's output and breaks AC10 - and because the collision depends on orangetrack having a short whole-bold paragraph in some fixture (unmeasured), it may pass CI today and drift in production. The Testing Strategy contains no assertion in either direction.
findings.recommendation:
Make the heuristic a fourth injected policy, opt-in per source: BlockBuilder(..., bold_heading=False) with t-hunted/lamley passing True and orangetrack/autoevolution keeping the default. Tests (all in the NEW tests/test_dom_blocks.py, so the unedited rule is not violated): (a) test_bold_heading_heuristic_is_off_by_default - build a default BlockBuilder, walk '

Short Bold Title

', assert blocks[0]['type'] == 'paragraph' and 'level' not in blocks[0]; (b) test_bold_heading_heuristic_promotes_when_enabled - same input with bold_heading=True, assert type == 'heading' and level == 3; (c) test_orangetrack_does_not_promote_bold_paragraphs - call orangetrack_source._parse_content_encoded('

Just A Bold Line

Body text here.

', link) and assert [b['type'] for b in out['blocks']] == ['paragraph', 'paragraph']; (d) the same for autoevolution via _scrape_article_page, since its exact block-type sequence assertion at tests/test_autoevolution_source.py:139-152 is the tripwire and its whole-bold lead div (class 'sanscond ... bold', fixture line 25) is exactly the shape at risk.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (Unit tests, dom_blocks bullet 1)
findings.issue: The heading heuristic has positive controls only - the same one-sided-invariant failure as 2026-07-28. Listed: whole-bold -> heading; whole-bold ending '.' -> NOT heading; ellipsis/'?'/'!' -> heading. Since Decision 2 removed the length limit, the discriminating condition is now 'whole' - and there is no test for a paragraph that is bold but NOT wholly bold. Four load-bearing negatives are absent, including the one the mechanics most likely get wrong: II-2.4 specifies the predicate as 'merge bold spans, require exactly ONE merged span, require text[:start].strip()=="" and text[end:].strip()==""', so a multi-span fully-covered paragraph must NOT promote.
findings.recommendation:
Replace the three bullets with a parametrised table (html, expected_type) in tests/test_dom_blocks.py, named so `pytest -k heading_heuristic` selects it (user-spec AVP step 3 depends on that selector). Required rows - POSITIVE: '

Treasure Hunts e Super Treasure Hunts

' -> heading; '

Todo Hot Wheels antigo e valioso?

' -> heading; '

Title

' (surrounding whitespace only) -> heading; a 140-char whole-bold paragraph -> heading, with a docstring naming Decision 2's removal of the length limit as deliberate so a future re-introduction of a cap fails this test. NEGATIVE: '

Bold lead-in and then ordinary prose continues here.

' (partially bold, short) -> paragraph; '

Part and two

' (two spans covering everything but a plain middle) -> paragraph; '

Ford vs Ford

' (run text occurs twice - the text.find span-merge must not conclude full coverage) -> paragraph; '

“Title”

' (quote chars outside the span) -> paragraph; '

Ends with a period.

' -> paragraph. Assert on blocks[0]['type'] and on 'level' presence, not on text.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (Integration tests, 'Count mismatch => blocks dropped, article published, WARNING logged') + Task 8
findings.issue: The AC8 guard is specified with the firing case only, is reachable only through a fabricated dict, and its output shape is unpinned. (1) No false-positive control: a guard that fires on every article silently disables the whole feature on 100% of publications and passes every test listed - the higher-probability bug, since the counting set is ('lead','paragraph','heading','list_item') and list_item was only just added to the engines. (2) Not naturally reachable: after Wave 2 the parsers are aligned by construction, and code-research II-3.3 notes orangetrack satisfies the invariant by construction so 'the guard cannot be tested through orangetrack' - leaving a hand-built dict as the only listed path. (3) II-3.3 requires blocks be set to None, not [], because the distinction is live and tested (tests/test_pending_articles_repo.py:276-287) and hw_review's parity gate at hw_review.py:396-404 treats [] as 'has blocks'; the strategy says only 'dropped'.
findings.recommendation:
Four tests. (a) test_alignment_guard_does_not_fire_on_aligned_article - real t-hunted fixture through fetch_t_hunted_article then news_bot row assembly; assert row['blocks'] equals the parser's list unchanged AND `assert not [r for r in caplog.records if r.levelno >= logging.WARNING]`. (b) test_alignment_guard_reached_naturally_via_title_dedup - II-3.2 names the second divergence source: t_hunted_source.py:198 / lamley_source.py:390 skip a tag whose text == title while the walker has no such check, so a fixture whose first

repeats the article title produces one block with no flat counterpart and drives the guard end-to-end through the real parser. Assert row['blocks'] is None and exactly one WARNING containing the link and both counts. This test also covers the title-dedup divergence, which the Testing Strategy does not mention at all. (c) test_guard_sets_blocks_to_none_not_empty_list - `assert row['blocks'] is None` explicitly. (d) test_guard_counts_list_item_as_patchable - article with 2 paragraphs + 2 list_items + 4 flat entries must NOT fire; drop one flat entry and it must fire.

findings.location: Task 4 (Files to modify) + Section: Testing Strategy (no engine entry at all)
findings.issue: AC3's behavioural half has no test anywhere, and three of four changed modules get no test. Verified: `grep -rn '_PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES|list_item' tests/test_claude_transcreation.py tests/test_gemini_transcreation.py tests/test_openai_transcreation.py tests/test_openrouter_transcreation.py` returns nothing - zero references in all four files. Task 4 edits claude_transcreation.py:159, gemini_transcreation.py:132, openai_transcreation.py:129, openrouter_transcreation.py:217 but lists only tests/test_claude_transcreation.py. The Testing Strategy's Unit and Integration sections contain no engine item at all, so AC3's requirement that list items are not re-translated by the second call is asserted nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Add the three missing engine test files to Task 4. Write one parametrised-over-engines behavioural test: patch the engine client, call the second-pass translator (the loop at claude_transcreation.py:181-192 and its three twins) with skip_patched_text=True and blocks=[{'type':'list_item','text':'Уже по-русски','runs':[{'text':'Уже','formats':['bold']}]}, {'type':'image','src':'https://x/1.jpg','caption':'Photo: Mattel'}]. Assert: (1) 'Уже по-русски' does NOT appear in the outbound user message captured from the mocked client - the assertion that fails today and passes after the fix; (2) 'Photo: Mattel' DOES appear (false-positive control: the caption pass must still run - a test that only checks absence also passes if the second call is disabled entirely); (3) the returned list_item text is unchanged; (4) the list_item's runs survive. Add a drift guard alongside: for each engine module `assert engine._PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES == _llm_common._PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES` - one line that prevents the four-way divergence this task fixes from recurring.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy (E2E tests: None) + Integration tests ('a gallery-heavy lamley fixture (the measured 50-image case)')
findings.issue: E2E-as-live-fetch is correctly excluded (autoevolution article pages 403, lamley 20 s + 24 h blacklist), but the chosen substitute - 'the operator's side-by-side comparison after deploy' - is a human post-deploy check, not a test. The missing artefact is a recorded-fixture corpus, which needs no network at test time. tests/fixtures/ contains only mattel_flight_builder.py and cross_source_dedup_pairs.py: zero HTML. Consequence: every load-bearing measurement in this spec is unreproducible once the research session ends - 24 promotions across 286 paragraph blocks, longest accepted heading 73 chars vs shortest rejection 85, lamley image blocks 14/41/48/50, 13-of-14 misalignment, flat-text drift -0.10%/-1.18%. The integration test is written against 'the measured 50-image lamley fixture', which does not exist in the repo. All planned unit tests therefore run on hand-written snippets shaped by the same assumptions they are meant to verify.
findings.recommendation: Make recorded fixtures mandatory as a Wave 1 deliverable (extend Task 1 or add Task 1b): commit tests/fixtures/articles/{t_hunted,lamley,orangetrack,autoevolution}/<slug>.html - the 14 already-fetched pages trimmed to the body container, plus the orangetrack content:encoded snapshot II-2.4 says was never pulled. .dockerignore already excludes tests/, so prod image size is unaffected. Then convert the measurement into a deterministic pytest module tests/test_real_article_corpus.py with exact expected values: heading promotions per article equal a committed expected set (not just a count); lamley image-block counts == [14, 41, 48, 50]; after the aligned lift, patchable-block count == len(paragraphs) on 14/14; per-article flat-text delta within the measured envelope. This corpus is also the golden input for finding 1 and the honest input for the AVP's preview_renderer check.

findings.location: Section: Agent Verification Plan ('re-runs the measurement script from code-research.md Part II against live t-hunted articles')
findings.issue: A network-dependent, non-deterministic step is not acceptable in a pre-deploy gate. (1) It fails for reasons unrelated to the change - and this project has a logged incident where an outage alarm turned out to be server DNS, so a network failure here will be misattributed. Blocking a deploy on it is costlier than usual because deploys are barred 10:00-20:00 MSK, so a spurious failure costs a day. (2) It has no fixed expected value: t-hunted's feed content changes, so 'still scores as measured' can only be evaluated by judgement, which is not a gate outcome. (3) CI runs `python -m pytest tests/ -v` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:42); a step CI cannot run is a manual ritual, not a gate.
findings.recommendation: Split it. Pre-deploy: run the measurement over the committed corpus from the previous finding, with exact expected counts, as an ordinary pytest module - deterministic, offline, CI-runnable, and it fails loudly if classification changes. Post-deploy (Task 14): keep the live t-hunted re-run as informational drift monitoring, with an explicit AVP rule that a network/fetch failure is INCONCLUSIVE and never a fail, and that a classification change on newly published articles opens a follow-up rather than blocking. State in the AVP that no pre-deploy step may touch the network.

findings.location: Decision 5 + Section: Testing Strategy ('Image cap: blocks path emits no more than the cap, hero preserved')
findings.issue: AC9 names two different caps (30 t-hunted, 10 lamley) but the only specified assertion is a one-sided upper bound on one source. telegraph_publisher.py has no IMAGE_LIMIT constant (verified) - the caps live in the four parsers (t_hunted:49, lamley:93, autoevolution:39, orangetrack:73), so putting the cap inside the source-agnostic _build_content_from_blocks means the value must travel parser -> row -> publish_article -> preview_nodes -> renderer. Nothing tests that plumbing, and 'no more than the cap' passes if the implementation hard-codes 10 for everyone - which would silently truncate t-hunted galleries (measured max 27 images) on 100% of gallery posts while every listed test stays green. There is no lower control and no boundary case.
findings.recommendation: Three tests in tests/test_telegraph_publisher.py plus one integration test. (a) test_image_cap_is_per_source_not_global - the same 50-image block list rendered twice: cap=10 -> 10 image nodes, cap=30 -> 30; assert both, so a single hard-coded value fails. (b) test_t_hunted_27_image_article_is_not_capped - 27 image blocks with cap=30 -> all 27 figure nodes survive (the lower control that catches over-capping). (c) test_hero_survives_cap_of_one - cap=1 with 5 image blocks -> exactly one figure node, and it is the first image block (Decision 5's 'keeping the hero'); cap=0 must not raise. (d) Integration: drive news_bot._fallback_publish with a t-hunted row and a lamley row carrying identical 50-image block lists and assert the surviving image-node counts differ (30 vs 10) - the only assertion that proves the cap value actually arrives from the row instead of defaulting.

findings.location: Section: Agent Verification Plan + Section: Testing Strategy (AC6 markers_lost and AC7 bold_heavy absent)
findings.issue: The user-spec's 'Kak proverit' table - which the AVP names as its source - drives five of eleven steps through `pytest -k` selectors: heading_heuristic, mismatch, markers_lost, bold_heavy, flag_off, image_limit. AC6 and AC7 name markers_lost and bold_heavy as required tests, and AC6 additionally fixes the assertion ('v send_admin_notification ne bylo vyzovov'). Neither name appears anywhere in the tech-spec Testing Strategy, and no task's file list clearly owns them. This matters mechanically: `pytest -k <nothing-matches>` collects zero items and exits 0, so a mis-named test turns an AVP step into a guaranteed silent pass. Five of eleven verification steps are vacuous by default.
findings.recommendation: List the six required selector substrings in the Testing Strategy and assign each to a task: heading_heuristic -> Task 1; flag_off -> Task 3; markers_lost, bold_heavy, mismatch, image_limit -> Task 8 (markers_lost/bold_heavy may sit in Task 5/6 per source). Spell out the two AC-mandated assertions: markers_lost - feed a RU translation with no ** markers for one block, assert the block publishes as plain text AND the send_admin_notification mock has call_count == 0 (not merely 'not called with X'); bold_heavy - an article with >=90% of its text inside bold runs, assert the count of strong nodes in the rendered tree equals the count of bold runs in the blocks, i.e. nothing was suppressed by a hidden threshold. Add tests/test_avp_selectors.py running pytest --collect-only -q -k '<selector>' for each of the six and asserting >=1 item collected - the cheap guard against zero-collected-equals-pass.

findings.location: Section: Testing Strategy ('Kill switch: flag off => no blocks key emitted by any of the three parsers') + Decision 6 + Task 3
findings.issue: One-sided and structurally incomplete, with one behavioural trap unaddressed. (1) No ON-side control: 'flag off => no blocks' passes if the flag is stuck off or if block emission never works at all - the litmus test fails outright. (2) No value-parsing coverage, although code-research II-5.1 documents the exact convention both precedents set (off-words 0/false/no/off, unset -> ON, unrecognised 'maybe' -> ON) and both carry comments warning that const-vs-env-name drift makes a 'dark' deploy a silent no-op. (3) The trap: Decision 6 and Task 3 put the flag inside dom_blocks.py, and orangetrack is dom_blocks' first consumer (Task 1). If the flag gates emission inside the shared module, flag-off strips orangetrack's blocks too - a regression on a source that works today, and a violation of AC10 in the flag-off state. Nothing in the strategy asserts orangetrack is unaffected by the flag.
findings.recommendation: Five assertions in tests/test_dom_blocks.py. (a) Flag ON (default) => each of the three parsers returns a non-empty 'blocks' list on a fixture with markup - the ON-side control. (b) Flag OFF => `assert 'blocks' not in out` for all three (not `assert not out.get('blocks')`, since [] and None are distinguished downstream). (c) Flag OFF => orangetrack still returns its blocks unchanged: parametrise over the golden fixtures and assert equality against the golden file from finding 1. (d) Parse table: parametrise ('', '1', 'true', 'YES', 'on', 'maybe', '0', 'false', 'no', 'off', ' Off ') -> expected bool, matching news_bot.py:134-136 semantics exactly. (e) Assert the constant name equals the env-var string literal - the const/env drift guard both precedents comment on. Patch the module global (`patch('dom_blocks.FLAG', False)`) per the project's existing test convention rather than mutating os.environ.

findings.location: Section: Agent Verification Plan ('Source: user-spec Kak proverit section')
findings.issue: The AVP cites the user-spec checklist as its source without restating it, but two of that checklist's expected results were invalidated by operator-approved deviations recorded in this same tech-spec. Row 3 expects '80 simvolov - zagolovok, 81 - net', deleted by the Decision 2 deviation (length condition removed entirely). Row 9 expects 'S vyklyuchennym flagom vyvod identichen dofix-povedeniyu', contradicted by the Decision 6 deviation (flag-off is explicitly NOT byte-identical; measured drift -0.10% / -1.18%). A verifier following the cited source will either write a test that cannot pass or record a false pass against a superseded expectation.
findings.recommendation: Restate rows 3 and 9 inside the tech-spec AVP with corrected expectations and a note that they supersede the user-spec. Row 3: whole-bold AND not ending in '.', regardless of length; verified by the parametrised heading table including the multi-span and partially-bold negatives. Row 9: flag off => `'blocks' not in result` for all three parsers, orangetrack's blocks unchanged, and flat-text length within the measured -0.1% / -1.2% envelope - assert a bound, not equality.

findings.issue: _build_content_from_blocks ignores runs for 'lead' blocks (research II-8.4, re-verified as still present), and autoevolution is the only lead producer. Task 7 swaps in the shared walker, so autoevolution's lead div (class 'sanscond mgtop_20 fsz22 bold', tests/test_autoevolution_source.py:25) starts carrying bold runs that the renderer silently discards. AC1 ('bold from the original is visible in Telegraph, for autoevolution') is then partially unmet, and no test records the fact either way.
findings.recommendation: Either fix and pin, or document and pin - but assert something. Fix: route lead through _render_paragraph_with_runs like paragraph, and add test_lead_block_renders_runs asserting the node tree contains an inner format tag for a lead with a bold run. Document: test_lead_block_runs_are_deliberately_not_rendered asserting the lead renders as a single flat paragraph with no inner strong node, with a docstring naming research II-8.4 - so the gap is a recorded decision rather than a latent surprise for whoever verifies AC1 on autoevolution.

findings.location: Solution paragraph ('exactly one real policy hook (_has_color_class)') vs Architecture ('three injected callables')
findings.issue: The spec is internally inconsistent about whether the WordPress colour-class bold rule is per-site policy or a shared default: the Solution calls _has_color_class the one real policy hook of _runs_from_tag, while the Architecture's injection list (chrome predicate, image-src picker, video wrapper) does not contain it. If it becomes a shared default, a Blogger or autoevolution span matching the pattern invents bold the original never had - and, combined with the heuristic, can invent a heading. Same 'bold appears where it should not' failure class as finding 3, one layer down, with no test in either direction.
findings.recommendation: Add test_color_class_bold_is_opt_in_per_source to tests/test_dom_blocks.py: feed a paragraph containing a colour-classed span through a default-policy BlockBuilder and assert the resulting run has NO 'formats' key; then with the orangetrack policy object assert formats == ['bold']. Pair it with a t-hunted/lamley fixture containing such a span, asserting no bold reaches the blocks. orangetrack's own test_color_class_emits_bold_format (tests/test_orangetrack_source.py:1261) must keep passing unedited, so the negative side has to live in the new file.

findings.location: Risks table (promo-filter row and test_deploy_files_invariant row) vs Section: Testing Strategy and Task list
findings.issue: Two Risks-table mitigations are promised as tests but appear in no Testing Strategy entry and no task. (a) 'Test pins a case where chrome sits at the head' for the promo-filter risk (_is_promo_article reads the first 8 paragraphs; lamley loses 4-5 chrome entries, admitted 'not guaranteed in general') - orphaned, owned by nobody. (b) The deploy-files row says Task 1 adds dom_blocks.py to tests/test_deploy_files_invariant.py, but research II-8.5 shows that test only substring-searches for the literal '"t_hunted_source.py"' (line 24) and enumerates nothing - so the added entry passes for the wrong reason and the invariant its own docstring claims stays unenforced for the next module too.
findings.recommendation: (a) Assign the head-chrome test explicitly to Task 6 (lamley) and Task 5 (t-hunted): fixture with WordPress/Blogger chrome as the first two entries; assert the first 8 flat paragraphs after filtering match the pre-change set AND that _is_promo_article returns the same verdict on old and new flat text - a paired assertion, not a one-sided one. (b) Rewrite test_deploy_files_invariant.py to enumerate first-party modules actually imported by news_bot.py (walk the AST for top-level imports, exclude stdlib and site-packages) and assert each appears in deploy.sh's FILES array; add that rewrite to Task 1's scope.
